ruleName: Deliberate Actions to Affect Ball in Motion
title: Lifting Equipment Likely to Interfere with Ball in Motion
question: On the putting green, Jezz hits a putt too hard. Alison picks up Jezz's wedge left on the green before the ball hits the club. What is the ruling?

choices.text: Both Alison and Jezz receive the general penalty.

explanation: Under Rule 11.3, equipment that could affect where a ball might come to rest may be lifted or moved while the ball is in motion. Alison is permitted to remove the wedge before the ball reaches it and there is no penalty.

juniorVersion.title: Picking Up a Club on the Green While the Ball is Rolling
juniorVersion.question: Jezz hits her ball too hard on the green. Alison sees that Jezz's wedge is lying on the green and might get in the way. Alison quickly picks up the wedge before the ball gets there. What should happen?

choices.text: Both Alison and Jezz get a penalty.

juniorVersion.explanation: No one gets a penalty. It's okay to pick up something, like a wedge, to stop it from getting in the way of a moving ball.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The smooth grassy area around the hole where you putt the ball.
A type of golf club used for short shots.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Remind young golfers they can move clubs or other things if they think a rolling ball might hit them.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids might think you can't touch anything while a ball is moving.
Kids might think someone will always get a penalty if they touch equipment when a ball is rolling.
